INVENTORY AND IMPACT

Applicable obligations and potential harm are different questions

13 / 29

Which duties apply?

The obligations and supervisory expectations relevant to this use.

What harm is possible?

Who could be harmed, how severely, how likely, and whether it can be corrected.

Compare two uses in the same retailer.

  • Drafting a meeting summary. An employee checks it before circulating, so the effect is contained.
  • Automatically refusing refunds. This directly affects customers, so the decision and review arrangements need closer examination.

A voluntary framework label does not tell an approver which use presents the greater risk.

Legal applicability and potential harm answer different questions. Identify the duties and expectations relevant to the use. Assess who could be harmed, its severity and likelihood, and whether it can be corrected. Both assessments help determine the controls and approval authority required.

Compare two hypothetical uses within the same retailer. An employee uses AI to draft an internal meeting summary, then checks it before circulation. Another system automatically refuses customer refunds using order histories and complaint records. Both can involve personal data, but their effects and operating safeguards differ. The second use can directly affect customers and requires closer examination of the decision and review arrangements. A voluntary framework label alone does not tell the approver which use presents the greater risk.
